name: Fundamentals of Biomechanics
description: Biomechanics of human movement, qualitative analysis, nine fundamentals of biomechanics, musculoskeletal systems, musculoskeletal biomechanics: range-of-motion principle, force-motion principle, force analysis, Hill muscle model, muscle-tendon unit, force-velocity, force-length, force-time relation, force analysis, cardiovascular anatomy and physiology, blood and its components, cardiovascular biomechanics - Poiseuille's flow, fluid flow - Newtonian and non-Newtonian flows, Navier-Stokes, cardiac parameters, ECG, respiratory biomechanics: anatomy and physiology of human respiratory system, compliance and resistance, RC equivalence of lungs, effects of aging, acoustic biomechanics and hearing: anatomy and physiology of human ear, basics of acoustics, mechanics of hearing, biomechanics of vision: mechanics of visual system, refraction, refractive errors: myopia, hyperopia, and astigmatism. Biomechanics of digestive system: gastro-intestinal tract, enzymes and digestion mechanism, neurobiomechanics: central and peripheral neural system, neuro-muscular physiology, action potential, motor control, EEG, neuro plasticity, neuro-muscular disorders.
